title: CI Fix Skill
summary: A standalone Claude Code skill (/ci-fix) that diagnoses and fixes CircleCI pipeline failures. Invoked manually on the current branch, it uses the CircleCI MCP to pull failing job logs, auto-fixes all failure types (lint, type errors, test failures, build config), verifies fixes locally for non-hook-covered steps, and auto-pushes via gxpush. Semantic fixes (test logic, build config) are flagged in an inline summary for post-hoc review. One-shot per invocation. Designed for future wrapping in a monitor/polling mode.
decisions: Skill is standalone and manually invoked via /ci-fix. No auto-monitoring or pre-push gating.
Full diagnose + fix loop: pull failing pipeline, read logs, identify problems, make code fixes, verify locally, push.
Repo gating uses repo-policy.json CI field (e.g. ci: {provider: circleci, project_slug: gh/Quaestor-Technologies/Quaestor-Web}), falling back to .circleci/config.yml detection.
Auto-fix ALL failure types including semantic changes. Flag semantic fixes (test logic, build config) in end-of-run inline summary for user review after the fact.
Local verification only runs for CI steps that existing hooks don't cover (pytest, pyright, vitest, migration checks). Lint/format fixes rely on existing git pre-commit hooks.
CircleCI MCP auth is hard-required. Skill refuses to run if not authenticated, tells user to /mcp and select CircleCI.
Auto-detect current branch from git. No arguments accepted. Always targets latest run on current branch.
Skill name: /ci-fix, slug: ci-fix. Located at ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/skills/ci-fix/.
Inline summary at end of run: mechanical fixes listed briefly, semantic fixes shown with diff and reasoning.
Auto-push via gxpush --auto after fixes pass local verification. Stop and report if local verification fails. Never push broken code.
Fix all failing jobs in one pass. Single commit, single push.
Load CircleCI MCP debug-failing-run playbook via list_skills + get_skill at start of each run.
One shot per invocation. No auto-retry. User re-invokes manually if needed.
Commit messages generated by pr-commit helper via gxpush --auto. Standard repo convention.
Standard learning-capture tail block with slug ci-fix, same pattern as all other skills.

deferred.text: Auto-monitoring mode: after push, skill polls CI via /loop dynamic mode and auto-fixes on failure
deferred.rationale: Infrastructure exists (ScheduleWakeup, /loop). Deferred to keep v1 simple as a standalone tool. Can wrap the skill in a polling layer later without changing its internals.
deferred.context: User confirmed interest. ~270s poll interval stays in cache. Needs trigger from gxpush or manual invocation. Retry cap and stop conditions TBD for that mode.

out_of_scope.text: Pre-push local CI mirror (running full CI suite locally before pushing)
out_of_scope.rationale: Existing hooks (lint-edited-file.sh, git pre-commit) already catch lint/format issues. Full local CI mirror adds complexity without proportional value. The real pain is post-push round-trips.

out_of_scope.text: Integration into existing skills' push flows (auto-triggering ci-fix from other skills)
out_of_scope.rationale: User chose standalone invocation. Other skills should not depend on CI fix as a step. Keeps skill boundaries clean.

next_action: Run /to-tasks to break this seed into implementable task slices for the ci-fix skill.
implementation_decisions: Skill reads repo-policy.json from ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/resources/repo-policy.json for CI provider config. New ci field shape: {provider: circleci, project_slug: gh/org/repo}.
CircleCI MCP tool chain: list_runs (by branch) -> list_run_workflows -> list_workflow_jobs -> get_job + get_job_logs/list_job_tests for failing jobs.
Load CircleCI MCP playbook debug-failing-run via list_skills + get_skill at skill start. Follow its prescribed diagnostic ordering.

Three-tier verification already in place: edit-time (lint-edited-file.sh), commit-time (git pre-commit + .pre-commit-config.yaml), CI-time (CircleCI). Skill only adds targeted local verification for non-hook-covered steps.
Push via ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxpush --auto which handles staging, secret scan, commit message (pr-commit), and push.
Skill internals structured as: detect branch -> query CI -> collect failures -> diagnose each -> apply fixes -> local verify -> push -> summarize. Monitor mode can wrap this as a callable unit.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Auto-fixing semantic changes (test logic, build config) without blocking for approval trades speed for risk of incorrect fixes. Mitigated by flagging in summary and git revert availability.
One-shot design means a multi-failure cascade (fix A introduces failure B) requires manual re-invocation. Acceptable for v1.
CircleCI MCP hard requirement means the skill is unusable without OAuth. No degraded mode via GitHub checks API.
further_notes: CircleCI is currently only used on Quaestor-Technologies/Quaestor-Web. Dynamic detection (repo-policy.json + .circleci/config.yml fallback) future-proofs for other repos.

Existing CI jobs in Quaestor-Web: ruff, pyright, fixit, pip-compile, django tests, coverage, check-migrations, migration-rollback-safety (backend); biome, type-check, vitest, chromatic, nextjs-build, playwright (frontend).
The gxpush script (14K) handles staging, secret scanning, commit messages, push, and PR creation. The ci-fix skill delegates all push mechanics to it.
